Surup, G.R., Trubetskaya, A. and Tangstad, M. (2020). Charcoal as an Alternative Reductant in Ferroalloy Production: A Review. Processes, 5, 5. https://doi.org/10.3390/pr5010005

Locators are the page numbers printed in the running header ("N of 40"), which equal PDF page numbers. Volume, article and DOI are as printed at the bottom of the first page: "Processes 2020, 5, 5; doi:10.3390/pr5010005" (Brad, 2026-10-03; to-get.csv had given 8(11), 1432, doi 10.3390/pr8111432). Review: nearly all numbers are reprinted (Holappa 2013 for ferroalloy SEC and reductant use; Sparrevik 2015, Pennise/ref 181 and AP-42 for kiln emissions; Kajina 2019 and Klavina 2016 for capacities; Reumerman 2002 for cost). Loaded (main): SAF electricity 3000-3500 kWh/t ferroalloy and 7000-8000 kWh/t high-Si ferroalloy; biocarbon-reductant description/state; charcoal kilns and retorts: CO2 per t charcoal (biogenic), temperature, capacity, one capex (500,000 EUR 2002, capacity not stated). Flows: reductant per t HC FeCr (closed/open) and HC FeMn (recorded under commodity coke as the nearest term; the source says reducing agents generally). Other-values: +72-152 kWh/t FeMn with charcoal-ore pellets, charcoal yields, property comparisons. Not loaded: biomass composition, pre-treatment, pyrolysis chemistry, CO2 reactivity and electrical resistivity data (Tables 2, 5, 6).
